title: One tool answers whether a head merges clean with main and another head
why: Triage (2026-11-11 08:49 CST) checked #2378 and #1166 against main with `T=$(git merge-tree ... | head -1) && echo clean`, which reads head's exit code, so two conflicted merges read clean. Two builders then hit conflicts their briefs called clean. Harm: wasted lanes and wrong briefs. Fix: a `merge --merge-check <pr> [--with <sha>]` read mode (or a bin script) that prints clean or the conflicted files from merge-tree's own exit, and hand-over briefs cite it. INCIDENT 21:40 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 21:38, runner 10's read; triage read none): a #3242 ready run was lost, 50 min, on a conflict in merge/merge.py that a merge-tree read against main and the other ready PRs before the mark would have shown. Want (coordinator): runner 10 reads a merge-tree of each head against main and the ready PRs before a mark. This step's tool (one answer to "does this head merge clean with main and another head") is the home for that read; the runner uses it before the mark. Kin: release-pairwise-clash (release set), lane-lint-names-clashing-open-pr. Filed as an extension here, not a new step (rule building-one-home-per-capability).
